blocks.content: The primary objective of the Central Information Commission is to ensure transparency, accountability, and the effective enforcement of the Right to Information Act.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Information Commission (CIC) was constituted in 2005 under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
The primary objective of the CIC is to enforce the right to information and foster transparency and accountability in governance.
It acts as the final appellate authority for RTI appeals and inquires into complaints regarding non-furnishing of information.
The Commission exercises quasi-judicial powers equivalent to a civil court while conducting inquiries under the RTI Act.
CIC is a Statutory Body created under the RTI Act, 2005, and NOT a Constitutional Body.
The Commission possesses the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure while inquiring into complaints.
The Annual Report of the CIC is submitted to the Central Government, which lays it before Parliament.
